questions.title: The Aura and the vanished creature

scenario.description: Your opponent controls a creature enchanted with Pacifism. You cast Naturalize targeting Pacifism. In response, your opponent activates an ability. That ability resolves and instructs them to sacrifice the enchanted creature.

question.prompt: What happens when Naturalize would resolve?

options.text: Naturalize doesn't resolve because its only target is illegal.
Naturalize resolves, but Pacifism remains on the battlefield.
The sacrificed creature returns to the battlefield.

questions.explanation: The sacrifice ability resolves first. After it finishes, state-based actions are checked before a player receives priority. Pacifism is no longer attached to a legal object, so it is put into its owner's graveyard. When Naturalize would resolve, its only target is no longer in the zone where it was targeted and is illegal. Because all of Naturalize's targets are illegal, it doesn't resolve. Players sometimes call this 'fizzling'; it is not the same as being countered by a counterspell.
questions.takeaway: An unattached Aura is put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action. A spell with all targets illegal doesn't resolve; that is often called fizzling, but it is not countered by a counterspell.

review.reviewer_type: Independent rule-text cross-check (AI-assisted; not judge certification)
review.notes: Scenario wording explicitly states the sacrifice is an effect on resolution, not an activation cost, to remove timing ambiguity. Checked against the cited Comprehensive Rules text effective September 25, 2026. Recheck before public launch or after a rules update.

editorial.intent: Test Aura state-based actions and what happens when all targets of a spell become illegal.
editorial.review_focus: Confirm the setup is clear, assumptions are complete, and only one answer is correct.
